meta.scope: Quad Cortex 'Guitar Amplifier' models: clean, edge-of-breakup and classic-crunch families (48 model ids, 20 families).

conventions.settings_values: Knobs are numbers on the QC range from the catalog (0..10 unless stated). Switches are true/false (true = on/engaged). Selectors are lowercase strings.
conventions.direction_fields: brighter / tighter / warmer say which way to move the control for that result: 'up', 'down' or 'n/a'. For switches 'up' means ON.
conventions.gain_range: Highest drive class the amp reaches by itself (no pedal): clean | edge | crunch | high. 'sweet_spot' is the class it is best known for.
conventions.basis: 'cited' = numbers taken from the source URL (converted to 0..10 where the note says so). 'typical' = synthesis of several sources; treat as a starting point.
conventions.OUTPUT: Every amp has OUTPUT[-60..12 dB]: a post-amp level trim (assumed tonally neutral). Use it for level-matching after VOLUME/GAIN has been set for feel; never as a tone or drive control.

scale_conversion.blackface_fender_1_to_10: Real blackface knobs read 1..10: qc = (n - 1) * 10 / 9. Example: real '6' = 5.6.
scale_conversion.tweed_fender_1_to_12: Real tweed knobs read 1..12: qc = (n - 1) * 10 / 11. Example: real '8' = 6.4.
scale_conversion.caveat: Several QC users report the models break up earlier than the real amps at the same knob number; use the numbers as ratios and aim by ear for 'just breaking up when I dig in'.

special_cases.text: Vox TONE CUT is a power-amp treble CUT: up = darker, down = brighter (Vox manual: 'the opposite of what you may think').
Matchless DC-30 CUT behaves like the Vox cut: up = darker; subtle below half, strong from half to full; most effective with MASTER high.
DC-30 Ch2 TONE is a 6-position thickness switch on the real amp: low = thin/bright, each step up = thicker. 'Brighter' = down.
Non-master-volume amps: VOLUME / GAIN is the only drive control and it drives preamp and power amp together. Change loudness with OUTPUT, not VOLUME.

On these circuits 'tighter' is mostly: lower BASS first, lower the Normal-channel volume on jumpered models, then a low-cut or mid-hump boost before the amp. More gain makes the low end looser, not tighter.
Bright switches/caps sit across the volume control: big effect at low VOLUME/GAIN, little or none near maximum. At low volume turn BRIGHT off before cutting TREBLE.

special_cases.applies_to: Fender, Marshall, Vox Top Boost, Matchless, Lone Star
special_cases.text: Passive stacks only cut and interact. Fender/Marshall: the scoop sits around 500 Hz; MID up fills it AND raises level/drive; Bass 0 / Mid 10 / Treble 0 is the flattest setting. Vox Top Boost: TREBLE up also cuts BASS; BASS up deepens the mid notch.

PRESENCE on tweed Fender / Marshall / Hiwatt circuits is a treble boost made by reducing high-frequency negative feedback in the power amp: it adds cut and edge after the preamp distortion, most audible when the amp is driven.
Mesa Lone Star PRESENCE is a high-frequency attenuator at the end of each channel's preamp: lower = darker AND more compressed/fatter (good for leads).
Lone Star GAIN and Dumble VOLUME shift the voicing as they rise: low = brighter, more upper harmonics; high = thicker, bassier, softer attack. As gain goes up, turn BASS down.

Patch/jumpered models blend a bright channel and a dark, bassy Normal channel. Brighter/tighter = less Normal volume; warmer/fatter = more Normal volume. Common advice: keep Normal at or below the bright volume.
Morgan SW50: the real amp's 'Level' (QC MASTER, assumed mapping) is power-section gain; past about 3 o'clock (8) it adds power-amp overdrive.
JC-120 is solid state and stays clean: requests for 'more drive/bite/compression' must be served by pedals or a compressor, not the amp.
Bogner pot tapers: treble at noon is roughly a Marshall's treble at 1. Running TREBLE at 7-9 is normal, not extreme.
CorOS 3.1.0 replaced US DLX Normal / US DLX Vibrato with US DLX 65 Reissue (1167) using MODE = Normal / Vibrato. Prefer 1167 for new presets.

Scooped, uncompressed amps (blackface Fender, Vox, JC-120) like mid-hump/compressed drives (Green 808, Rodent Drive). Mid-rich compressed amps (Marshall, Hiwatt) prefer flat boosts and fuzz (Fuzz Pi, Facial Fuzz); mid-hump drives can sound dark and boxy there.

unverified: Neural DSP publishes no per-parameter documentation: INPUT and MODE (1166/1167), BOOST (1011/1128), PREAMP and EQ (1176), EQ (1101-1108) and the 3 BRIGHT positions (1027) are interpreted from the real amps' panels and community posts.
Which of GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 is the bright channel on Patch models is inferred from Marshall panel convention (Volume I = High Treble, Volume II = Normal).
Whether the unused VOLUME NORMAL / VOLUME BRIGHT does anything on the non-Patch tweed models is not documented.
Matchless Chieftain BRILLIANCE direction rests on one forum post (up = brighter).
Morgan SW50: QC GAIN = amp Volume and QC MASTER = amp Level is an assumed mapping.
Very few QC-specific knob settings are published for these models; most 'cited' starts come from Yek's Fractal guide, manufacturer manuals and artist-settings pages.

families.real: Fender Deluxe Reverb (blackface AB763, 1963–67; '65 Reissue and hand-wired '64 Custom), 22 W, 2×6V6, 1×12
families.voice: Scooped mids, glassy sparkling top, soft 6V6 lows; chimey clean that sags and compresses into smooth breakup early.

VOLUME.does: Non-master: VOLUME is the gain. Breakup starts ~3-4 with single coils; 6+ is the classic 6V6 overdrive. Louder = looser lows.

TREBLE.does: Strongest tone control of the scooped stack; adds sparkle and deepens the scoop. No MID knob (fixed 6.8k mid resistor).

BASS.does: Feeds lows into a small 6V6 power amp: gets flabby once VOLUME is up. Lower BASS as VOLUME rises.

INPUT.does: 1166/1167 only. Assumed input-jack select (real amp: jack 2 is about 6 dB quieter = more headroom). Not documented.

MODE.does: 1166/1167 only. Channel select: 1167 = Normal / Vibrato. 1166 presumably the '64 Custom's Normal / Bright.

model_notes.1094: Normal channel: no bright cap, one gain stage fewer; darker and cleaner, good for jazz lines and humbuckers. Legacy id (now 1167 MODE=Normal).
model_notes.1095: Vibrato channel: fixed 47 pF bright cap plus an extra gain stage; the one most people use; breaks up earlier. Legacy id (now 1167 MODE=Vibrato).
model_notes.1166: '64 Custom Deluxe Reverb: hand-wired modified AB763 with Bright and Normal channels. Added in CorOS 3.1.0.
model_notes.1167: '65 Deluxe Reverb reissue. MODE Normal/Vibrato reproduces 1094/1095. Preferred id for new presets.

starts.name: cranked 6V6 overdrive
starts.note: ToneQuest via Yek: run it at '6' or above (1-10 dial = 5.6 here); guitar volume 10 for leads, back to ~7 to clean up. Keep BASS low.

boosts.why: Klon-style low-gain push adds the mids the scooped stack lacks without changing the amp's character; QC users run it at very low level.
Mid hump and compression fill the blackface scoop and trim the bass that makes the 6V6s flub.
Rat-type mids and compression suit scooped, uncompressed Fender-style amps.
QC forum users favour it (with Red Drive) for non-fizzy overdrive into the clean models.

cabs.why: The reissue's own 1×12 with Jensen C12K: glassy sparkle and attack.
Deluxe 1×12 with Eminence GA-SC64: alternative Deluxe speaker voicing.

known_for: Studio and club staple - 'on more recordings than any other Fender'
Country, blues, roots rock, soul, indie
Players listed for it: Duane Allman, Nile Rodgers, Dan Auerbach, John Scofield, Bill Frisell
families.poor_at: Loud clean headroom, tight low end and high gain: 22 W of 6V6 flubs on the low E when pushed; scooped mids vanish in a dense mix.
families.watch_out: The low E distorts first (lots of bass reaches the power amp; speaker resonance 50-100 Hz). Cut BASS to 2-3 or high-pass 75-100 Hz before the amp once VOLUME is above ~4.

families.real: Fender Twin Reverb (blackface AB763, 1963–67), 85 W, 4×6L6, 2×12
families.voice: Loud, piano-like clean: scooped mids, glassy to icy top, big firm lows; huge headroom and very little sag.

VOLUME.does: Non-master gain. The real amp stays clean to almost 6 where smaller Fenders break up at ~4; sounds thin when set very low.

BRIGHT.does: Bright cap across VOLUME: strong at low VOLUME, fades as VOLUME rises. Turn off if harsh or for squeaky-clean tones.

BASS.does: Plenty of lows on tap; turning it down keeps the amp tight and out of the bass guitar's range.

MID.does: Fills the mid scoop and raises level/drive. About 7 equals the fixed 6.8k mid of the smaller blackface amps.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control of the passive stack; adds glass and deepens the scoop.

model_notes.1083: Normal channel: no reverb-recovery stage, so it stays clean longest - the cleanest tube Fender here.
model_notes.1084: Vibrato channel: the extra stage of the reverb circuit makes it break up earlier than Normal.

boosts.why: Adds the midrange and compression this scooped, uncompressed amp lacks; the standard way to get lead tones from a Twin.
Rat-type distortion works on Fender-style scooped amps; the amp's headroom keeps it clear.
Low-gain mid push for edge-of-breakup without losing the Twin's clean punch.
Fat low end and strong mids suit mid-scooped amps.

cabs.why: The Twin Reverb's own open-back 2×12 with Jensens.
Twin 2×12 with Jensen C12K-2: efficient, glassy, big lows.
Fender cab with Celestion A-Type: rounder alternative if the Jensens are too icy.

known_for: The reference loud clean: country, jazz, funk, gospel, surf
Players listed for it: B.B. King, Johnny Marr, Eric Johnson (cleans), Steve Howe
Classic clean base for pedals
families.poor_at: Natural breakup at sane volume and mid-forward lead tones without a pedal; thin and icy when VOLUME is very low.
families.watch_out: Painfully bright and bass-heavy by default: turn BRIGHT off and BASS down before touching TREBLE, and get overdrive from a pedal, not from VOLUME.

families.real: Fender Super Reverb (blackface AB763, 1963–67; QC: '65), 40–45 W, 2×6L6, tube rectifier, 4×10
families.voice: Big scooped Fender with punchy 4×10 attack: deep lows, screaming treble, low mids; comes alive past ~4.

VOLUME.does: Non-master gain; the amp 'comes alive' beyond 4. More VOLUME also means more bass and sharper treble.

BRIGHT.does: Bright cap across VOLUME; effect fades as VOLUME rises. Often off for the SRV-style 'magic six'.

BASS.does: The big cabinet makes lots of deep bass; keep around 2-3 when VOLUME is up.

MID.does: Vibrato model only (Normal has a fixed mid). Fills the scoop and adds push; the cure for 'lost in the mix'.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control of the passive stack; 4×10s are beamy, so high settings get piercing fast.

model_notes.1096: Normal channel: no MID knob, no reverb-recovery stage; cleaner.
model_notes.1097: Vibrato channel: adds MID and an extra gain stage; the usual choice.

starts.name: magic six (SRV-style edge)
starts.note: Fenderguru's 'magic six' (6, 6, 2x3). Yek runs Bright off; the QC wiki copy lists Bright on. Model 1096 has no MID.

boosts.why: The classic Texas-blues pairing: mid hump fills the scoop, trims bass and pushes the 6L6s.
Transparent boost for more sustain and harmonics at the amp's sweet spot (fenderguru's suggestion).
Low-gain mid lift that keeps the Super's punch.

cabs.why: 4×10 Jensen P10R - the same speaker type Fender fits to the Super Reverb reissue.
Oxford alnico 10s: softer, earlier-breaking vintage Fender 10-inch voice.

known_for: Stevie Ray Vaughan-style Texas blues
Blues players: Muddy Waters, Mike Bloomfield, Robert Cray, Derek Trucks
Loud, warm 4×10 club tone
families.poor_at: Mid-rich or tight high-gain tones; beamy, scooped and bass-heavy, so it gets lost or boomy if you just add VOLUME.
families.watch_out: The scooped mids tempt you to turn up, which only adds more bass and sharp treble. Raise MID or add a mid-hump drive instead.

families.real: Fender Princeton Reverb (blackface AA1164, 1964–67), 12–15 W, 2×6V6, 1×10
families.voice: Small-box blackface: sweet chimey highs, punchy but soft lows; 'browner', mid-focused breakup that arrives early.

VOLUME.does: Non-master gain. With a Strat: 3-4 fairly clean, ~5 clean with balls, 7-8 trademark Fender overdrive.

TREBLE.does: Treble of a two-knob scooped stack (fixed 6.8k mid, no bright switch).

BASS.does: Dial it back: the small output section and 10-inch speaker fart out in the lows when pushed.

model_notes.1120: Reverb version: the reverb-recovery stage adds a gain stage, so it has more gain than a non-reverb Princeton.

starts.name: fairly clean (Strat)
starts.note: Yek: 'you only need to dial back Bass and adjust Input Drive... between 3 and 4 for a fairly clean tone'.

starts.name: clean with balls
starts.note: Fenderguru also plays the real amp at 5-6: single notes clean, chords crunchy.

starts.name: trademark Fender overdrive
starts.note: Yek: 'up to 7-8'. With humbuckers halve the input level first.

boosts.why: Small mid push into an amp already on the edge; keeps the recording-amp sweetness.
Cuts the lows that make the Princeton fart out and adds mids for leads.
Clean boost with bass/treble shaping to tip the amp over without adding pedal distortion.

cabs.why: Princeton 1×10 with Jensen C10R, an original speaker type.
Princeton 1×10 with a Fat Jimmy C1060: fuller alternative 10.
A 12 gives wider, deeper lows when the 10 sounds boxy.

known_for: Studio/recording amp played on the verge of breakup
Ryan Adams; players listed for it: Bill Frisell, St. Vincent, Mac DeMarco, Gary Clark Jr.
Ancestor of the Mesa/Boogie Mark I
families.poor_at: Clean headroom, tight bass and band-volume punch; the lows give up under heavy drive.
families.watch_out: With humbuckers it overdrives very early and muddy: cut the level into the amp (Yek halves the input) and lower BASS before judging it.

families.real: Fender Bassman 5F6-A (narrow-panel tweed, 1958–60; '59), 40–50 W, 2×6L6/5881, tube rectifier, 4×10
families.voice: Raw, fat, warm tweed: big loose lows, thick mids, bright bite on the Bright channel; touch-sensitive breakup - the Marshall template.

VOLUME NORMAL.does: Gain of the darker, fatter Normal channel. In Patch models it blends in body and lows.

VOLUME BRIGHT.does: Gain of the Bright channel (more treble, most at low settings). In Patch models it supplies the bite.

TREBLE.does: Interactive tweed stack after the gain stages. Reissue owners call it very bright; Bass 0 / Mid 10 / Treble 0 is the flat point.

BASS.does: It generates a lot of bass and flubs when driven: run 0-3. First control to cut for 'tighter'.

MID.does: Fills the ~500 Hz scoop and raises level/drive into the power amp; crank it for a thicker, pushier tone.

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp negative-feedback treble boost: adds cut and edge after the preamp, most audible when the amp is loud.

model_notes.1123: Jumpered, plugged into the Bright channel: both volumes are live.
model_notes.1124: Bright channel alone. Whether VOLUME NORMAL still does anything is not documented.
model_notes.1125: Jumpered, plugged into the Normal channel: both volumes are live.
model_notes.1126: Normal channel alone: darker and fatter. Whether VOLUME BRIGHT still does anything is not documented.

starts.name: forum 'secret' tone-stack setting
starts.note: Bass and Treble fully down, Mid and Presence at noon; volumes not given. Seen via search summary, not read in full.

starts.name: tweed crunch (Patch models)
starts.note: Follows Yek / QC wiki advice: crank mids, bass (almost) all the way down.

boosts.why: Yek: 'for some vintage fun, put the Face Fuzz before the amp' - the amp's compression smooths it.
A treble booster controls the amp's heavy low end while pushing it into drive.
Bass cut plus mid hump tightens the loose tweed lows for leads.
Low-gain push for edge-of-breakup without thinning the tweed mids.

cabs.why: The Bassman's own open-back 4×10 with Jensen P10R alnicos.
Blonde Bassman cab with Vintage 30s: tighter, more mid-forward for rock.

known_for: 'Grandfather of rock and roll' amps; the circuit Marshall copied for the JTM45
Blues, rock'n'roll, rockabilly, roots: Buddy Guy, Brian Setzer, Eric Clapton, Jimi Hendrix
Clean, funk, soul through to raw overdrive
families.poor_at: Tight palm-muted low end, glassy scooped cleans at volume, high gain.
families.watch_out: With BASS near noon it farts out as soon as the volume goes up: start with BASS at 0-2 and add MID instead.

families.real: Fender Twin 5F8-A 'high-powered' tweed Twin (1958–60), 80 W, 4×5881/6L6, 2×12
families.voice: Bassman-like but warmer, bigger and louder: dark, fat tweed clean with lots of headroom; compresses and fattens more than it distorts.

VOLUME NORMAL.does: Gain of the darker Normal channel; in Patch models it adds body. Keith Urban plugs into Normal.

VOLUME BRIGHT.does: Gain of the Bright channel. With single coils you must crank it to reach overdrive, and even then it mostly gets fatter.

TREBLE.does: Dark amp with its stock-style cab: run TREBLE higher than you would on a Bassman.

BASS.does: Turn it down; lots of lows from the tweed stack and 2×12 cabinet.

MID.does: Fills the scoop and adds push; Bonamassa-style settings run it nearly full.

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp feedback treble; turn it up along with TREBLE to open the dark voicing.

model_notes.1133: Jumpered, plugged into Normal: both volumes live.
model_notes.1135: Jumpered, plugged into Bright: both volumes live.

starts.name: Joe Bonamassa settings (converted from the 1-12 dials)
starts.note: Wiki lists Presence 6, Middle 11, Bass 1, Treble 8, Vol bright 10, Vol normal 1 on 1-12 dials (labelled 'Normal channel' there).

starts.name: fat clean (Patch models)
starts.note: Follows Yek: 'turn up Treble and Presence. And turn down Bass.'

boosts.why: The amp barely overdrives on its own with single coils; a mid-hump drive supplies gain and tightens the lows.
Its TREBLE control lifts the dark voicing while adding a little grit.
Bass and treble controls let you brighten and tighten a dark, fat amp while adding gain.

cabs.why: Tweed Twin 2×12 with Weber Classic alnicos - the matching cab in the catalog.
Keith Urban's Twin cab had Two-Rock speakers that sound close to G12-65s (Yek).

known_for: Keith Richards, Eric Clapton, Rory Gallagher, Joe Bonamassa, Keith Urban
Loud fat tweed clean for blues, roots rock and country
families.poor_at: Bright sparkle or real distortion by itself; with single coils it barely overdrives.
families.watch_out: It sounds dark with its matching cab: do not judge it at noon - raise TREBLE and PRESENCE and cut BASS first.

families.real: Vox AC30 (1959→; Top Boost early 1960s; QC panel matches the AC30 Hand-Wired), 30 W, 4×EL84 cathode-biased, no negative feedback, 2×12
families.voice: Chime and jangle with a forward upper-mid bite; compressed, harmonically rich EL84 breakup; lows go loose when cranked.

VOLUME.does: Non-master preamp gain. Real amp: jangly clean around 11-12 o'clock (4-5), light crunch from 2-3 o'clock (7-8).

TONE CUT.does: INVERTED. Power-amp treble cut: up = darker/smoother, 0 = brightest. Use it to tame fizz instead of TREBLE.

TREBLE.does: Top Boost model. Very interactive: raising TREBLE also cuts BASS. Start both at 5.

BASS.does: Top Boost model. More lows but also a deeper mid notch as it rises; low BASS = tighter and more midrange.

BOOST.does: Top Boost model. Assumed = Hand-Wired HOT mode: partly bypasses TREBLE/BASS for much more gain and mids.

BRIGHT.does: Normal model. Adds high-end sparkle to the darker, EQ-less Normal channel.

model_notes.1009: Normal channel: no tone stack, darker with fuller mids - the 'Brian May' sound, made for a treble booster. Only BRIGHT and TONE CUT shape it.
model_notes.1011: Top Boost channel: Bass/Treble stack with a midrange cut - the classic chimey AC30.

starts.name: light crunch (Top Boost), real-amp volume
starts.note: Top Boost volume ~2-3 o'clock where breakup begins; jangle clean 11 o'clock to noon. Via search summary; QC may break up earlier.

starts.name: Normal channel + treble booster lead
starts.note: Put Rage Booster in front.

boosts.why: The historic pairing: a treble booster adds gain and bite to the dark Normal channel and tightens the loose lows.
Boosting the input is the standard way to get more gain from a Vox; low-gain, keeps the chime.
Mid-hump drives suit the AC30's fixed-mid voicing and firm up the low end.

cabs.why: AC30 2×12 with Celestion alnico 'Silver Bell' drivers: the bright, chimey original voice.
AC30 with Greenbacks: warmer, woodier, less top - good when driven.
Open-back 2×12 with Alnico Golds: modern take on the alnico Vox voice with more headroom.

known_for: The Beatles and the British Invasion
Brian May (Queen), The Edge (U2), Rory Gallagher, Radiohead, Kings of Leon
Indie jangle and praise & worship edge-of-breakup tones
families.poor_at: Tight low end and big clean headroom; scooped modern or high-gain tones. No feedback loop, so the lows loosen when cranked.
families.watch_out: TONE CUT works backwards (up = darker). The scratchy top when driven is real: raise TONE CUT rather than killing TREBLE, which also shifts the bass and mids.

families.real: Vox AC15 (1958→; Top Boost), 15 W, 2×EL84 cathode-biased, no negative feedback, 1×12
families.voice: The AC30's little brother: same chime and upper-mid bite, but breaks up sooner with a softer, more compressed, smaller low end.

VOLUME.does: Non-master preamp gain; half the output tubes of an AC30, so the power amp gives up sooner.

TONE CUT.does: INVERTED. Power-amp treble cut: up = darker/smoother, 0 = brightest.

TREBLE.does: Top Boost model. Interactive: raising TREBLE also cuts BASS. Start both at 5.

BASS.does: Top Boost model. Adds lows and deepens the mid notch; keep low when driven.

BOOST.does: Top Boost model. Assumed = Hand-Wired HOT mode: partly bypasses the tone controls for more gain.

BRIGHT.does: Normal model. Adds top-end sparkle to the dark Normal channel.

model_notes.1127: Normal channel: no tone stack, darker and thicker; shape with BRIGHT, TONE CUT and a booster.
model_notes.1128: Top Boost channel: Bass/Treble stack and the classic chime.

boosts.why: Treble booster into an EL84 Vox: more gain and bite, less flub.
Input boost is the standard way to add gain to a Vox while keeping the chime.
Mid hump and bass cut firm up the small amp's loose low end.

cabs.why: The AC15's own 1×12 with a Celestion Alnico Blue.
Bigger 2×12 alnico Vox voice when the 1×12 sounds boxy.

known_for: The James Bond theme was recorded on an AC15
Studio-size Vox chime: British rock, indie, worship
Players listed for it: Brian May, The Edge, Rory Gallagher
families.poor_at: Headroom and low-end authority; tight or scooped high-gain tones.
families.watch_out: TONE CUT works backwards (up = darker), and it compresses early: for a cleaner sound lower VOLUME, do not just cut TREBLE.

families.real: Marshall JTM45 (model 2245, 1962–66), 30–45 W, KT66/5881, GZ34 rectifier; derived from the 5F6-A Bassman
families.drive_control: GAIN (the amp's volume; GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 on Patch)
families.voice: Tweed-like Marshall: warm, saggy, round crunch with thick mids and soft attack; less bite and tightness than a Plexi.

GAIN.does: The channel volume (no master): drives preamp and power amp together. High settings turn low notes muddy and fuzzy.

GAIN 1.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel I = High Treble: brighter and gainier. Verify by ear.

GAIN 2.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel II = Normal: dark and bassy; adds body. Keep at or below GAIN 1.

BASS.does: Bass-heavy circuit: players run it at 0-3, often fully off, to stop flub and fuzz.

MID.does: Stack sits after the gain stages: MID up fills the scoop and pushes the power amp harder.

TREBLE.does: Dominant control of the interactive stack; crank the tone controls for a warm overdriven blues tone.

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp negative-feedback treble: adds cut and a rawer edge, most audible when the amp is driven.

model_notes.1038: Normal channel: dark, bassy, no bright cap; fat blues tones - turn BASS way down.
model_notes.1039: High Treble channel: very bright and also bass-heavy; closest to a Super Lead.
model_notes.1040: Jumpered channels with two gains; the Bluesbreaker-style blend.

starts.name: Gary Moore-style (boosted)
starts.note: Fractal forum member Simeon via Yek: Input Drive 3, Presence 3, plus a TS808 with Drive 0, Tone 6, Level 7 (use Green 808).

boosts.why: Drive 0 / Level up trims the amp's heavy bass and pushes it into singing sustain (Gary Moore-style setting above).
1960s British pairing: a treble booster removes the flub and adds bite.
Mid-rich compressed Marshall-type amps smooth out fuzz pedals.
Clean-ish level push when you want the amp's own crunch at lower GAIN.

cabs.why: Late-60s Marshall 4×12 with G12M Greenbacks: the cab the amp was designed for.
Marshall 4×12 with Pulsonic Greenbacks: sweet mids, soft top.
Open-back 2×12 with pre-Rola Greenbacks: the closest thing here to a Bluesbreaker combo.
Marshall 4×12 with Alnico Creams: smoother, more touch-compressed vintage voice.

known_for: Eric Clapton on John Mayall's 'Beano' album (1966, Bluesbreaker combo)
British blues and blues-rock; Gary Moore-style leads
Marshall's first amp
families.poor_at: Tight, aggressive hard-rock crunch or metal: it has more sag and less crunch than later Marshalls and turns to mud with gain and bass up.
families.watch_out: In the real world nobody ran the volume high; with GAIN way up low notes go muddy and almost synth-like. Stay moderate, BASS near 0, and boost from the front.

families.real: Marshall Lead 50, model 1987 (plexi panel 1966–69, then JMP; '50-watt Plexi'), 50 W, 2×EL34
families.drive_control: GAIN (the amp's volume; GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 on Patch)
families.voice: Plexi roar that gives up sooner: a little more aggressive and compressed than the 100, with easier power-amp crunch.

GAIN.does: The channel volume (no master): the amp relies on power-amp distortion, so real crunch needs it well up.

GAIN 1.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel I = High Treble (bright cap, more gain). Verify by ear.

GAIN 2.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel II = Normal: dark, loads of bass. Keep at or below GAIN 1.

BASS.does: Run it very low, even 0 - especially on Normal and Patch models - or the low end flubs.

MID.does: Post-gain stack: MID up fills the scoop and adds push; 7-10 is normal for a Plexi.

TREBLE.does: Do not be afraid to run it very high, as on the real amp; dominant control of the stack.

PRESENCE.does: Treble boost from reduced negative feedback in the power amp: cut, rasp and looser feel; set to taste.

model_notes.1079: High Treble (Bright) channel: bright cap makes it borderline painful at low GAIN, mellowing as GAIN rises; the gainiest single channel.
model_notes.1081: Normal channel: flat, dark, loads of bass; turn BASS way down.

starts.name: typical Plexi EQ
starts.note: Fractal's Cliff Chase: 'Bass 2, Mid 8, Treble 7.5. Adjust Presence to taste.' Gain not specified.

starts.name: edge / cleans up with guitar volume (Bright)

boosts.why: Treble booster into a cranked Marshall: tightens the lows and adds singing gain.
The amp's compression smooths a Fuzz Face into the creamy 60s lead sound.
Level-up, gain-low boost trims bass and adds saturation for tighter leads; can turn boxy since the amp is already mid-rich.
Scooped Big Muff-type fuzz suits mid-rich, compressed British amps.

cabs.why: Marshall 4×12 with Pulsonic G12M Greenbacks: sweet mids, the period-correct pairing.
1969 tall 4×12 with G12M-25s: bigger low end, vintage top.
G12H30s: compress less than Greenbacks and are flatter - the 'Hendrix speaker' type.

known_for: Classic rock and hard rock crunch; the smaller sibling of the Super Lead
AC/DC- and early-70s-style rhythm tones
Players of Plexis generally: Hendrix, Page, Angus Young, Van Halen
families.poor_at: Clean headroom, tight modern low end and smooth highs: raspy by design and non-master, so it only sings when driven.
families.watch_out: Do not dial it like a master-volume amp: BASS at noon = flub. Run BASS 0-3 with MID and TREBLE high; the fizz on top is how a Plexi sounds.

families.real: Marshall Super Lead 100, model 1959 (1965→; plexi panel to 1969), 100 W, 4×EL34
families.drive_control: GAIN (the amp's volume; GAIN 1 / GAIN 2 on Patch)
families.voice: The classic-rock roar: bright, raspy, open and huge with upper-mid 'kerrang'; more headroom and punch than the 50.

GAIN.does: The channel volume (no master): power-amp distortion does the work; back the guitar volume off for a warm clean.

GAIN 1.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel I = High Treble (bright cap, more gain). Verify by ear.

GAIN 2.does: Patch model. By Marshall convention channel II = Normal: dark, loads of bass. Keep at or below GAIN 1.

BASS.does: Run it very low, even 0, or it gets flubby - most of all on the Normal channel.

MID.does: Post-gain stack: MID up fills the scoop and adds push; 8-10 is normal.

TREBLE.does: Run it high without fear, as on the real amp; dominant control of the stack.

PRESENCE.does: Treble boost from reduced negative feedback in the power amp; set to taste (JD Simo: 5-6).

model_notes.1091: High Treble (Bright) channel: boosted bright tone bordering on painful; its bright cap is also part of its gain.
model_notes.1093: Normal channel: flat response, dark, loads of bass.

starts.name: typical Plexi EQ
starts.note: Fractal's Cliff Chase: 'Bass 2, Mid 8, Treble 7.5. Adjust Presence to taste.' Gain not specified.

starts.name: JD Simo, Bright channel dimed
starts.note: From a Premier Guitar rig rundown as quoted by Yek: Bass 0, Mid 10, Treble 10, Volume 10, Presence 5-6.

starts.name: edge / cleans up with guitar volume (Bright)

boosts.why: The Hendrix recipe: the Plexi's compression smooths a Fuzz Face into a creamy lead.
Treble booster into a loud Marshall: tighter lows and more singing gain.
Level-up, gain-low boost trims bass and adds saturation for tighter leads; can turn boxy since the amp is already mid-rich.
Scooped Big Muff-type fuzz suits mid-rich, compressed British amps.

cabs.why: Marshall 4×12 with Pulsonic G12M Greenbacks: the stack sound.
1969 tall cab with G12M-25s: big lows, sweet vintage top.
G12H30s compress less and are flatter than Greenbacks - the 'Hendrix speaker' type.
Angled 1960A with G12M-25s: slightly more modern Greenback voice.

known_for: Jimi Hendrix, Jimmy Page, Pete Townshend, Angus Young, Eddie Van Halen (everything on 10, variac), Yngwie Malmsteen
The sound of classic and hard rock; the Marshall stack
families.poor_at: Clean headroom at the settings where it sounds best, tight modern low end, smooth highs; raspy and fizzy by design.
families.watch_out: Do not dial it like a master-volume amp: BASS at noon = flub. Run BASS 0-3 with MID/TREBLE high. Turning the bright channel down in gain also makes it thinner and harsher.

families.real: Hiwatt Custom 100 DR103 (late 1960s→; Harry Joyce-era 1970s), 100 W, 4×EL34
families.voice: Loud, hi-fi British clean: tight punchy lows, strong forward mids, glassy slightly hollow top; stiff, with crunch only when cranked.

GAIN.does: Channel volume. Gilmour keeps it around 2 o'clock (7) with a low master for a thick clean on the edge.

MASTER.does: Real master volume. Low = clean, tight pedal platform; crank it with GAIN for raw power-amp roar.

BASS.does: Wide-range and effective (unlike a Plexi's). Gilmour settings range from 2.5 to 8 depending on cab and era.

MID.does: Adds strong punch; the amp is already mid-forward. Gilmour settings span roughly 3 to 8.

TREBLE.does: Wide-range; Gilmour usually keeps it low (2-4) and gets clarity from PRESENCE.

PRESENCE.does: Subtle power-amp control: 'doesn't do a lot but it opens up the amp a little'.

model_notes.1063: Normal channel: voiced to stay clean and powerful at all levels; fuller and darker.
model_notes.1064: Brilliant channel: higher gain and brighter; the one that overdrives when pushed.

starts.name: Gilmour 2006 'On an Island' tour (clock positions converted)
starts.note: Real amp had linked inputs: Normal 2:00, Brilliant 1:00, Bass 11:00, Treble 10:00, Middle 1:30, Presence 3:00, Master 9:00. On the Bright model use GAIN 6.

starts.name: Gilmour 1994 tour (clock positions converted)
starts.note: Normal 2:00, Brilliant 1:00, Bass 9:30, Treble 10:30, Middle 12:00, Presence 3:00, Master 1:30. Starting point only; cab and tubes change everything.

starts.name: Yek's roar (Fractal model)
starts.note: 'Crank the Master. Bass is turned down and Presence between 3-4'; gain to taste. 'Bass 3' is my reading of 'turned down'.

boosts.why: Gilmour's Big Muff sound depends on a mid-rich, compressed Hiwatt to fill in and smooth the scooped fuzz.
Fuzz Face-type pedals turn smooth and creamy into darker British amps like a Hiwatt.
Flat/transparent boosts suit an amp that already has plenty of mids (the Powerboost role).

cabs.why: Hiwatt's own SE4123 4×12 - Hiwatt and Fane speakers go hand in hand.
Gilmour has also run a Marshall 4×12 alongside his WEM cab.

known_for: David Gilmour / Pink Floyd clean platform for fuzz and delay
Pete Townshend / The Who - 'Live at Leeds'
Players listed for it: Kevin Shields, Robert Fripp
families.poor_at: Easy low-volume breakup or saggy vintage feel: it is stiff and clean. Mid-hump drives (Green 808, Rodent Drive, Obsessive Drive) can sound dark and boxy into it.
families.watch_out: Do not expect a Plexi: at normal settings it stays clean. Use it as a loud clean base (GAIN ~7, MASTER low) and get the drive from a fuzz or flat overdrive in front.

families.real: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus (1975→), solid-state, 2×60 W stereo, 2×12
families.drive_control: none (VOLUME is level; the amp stays clean)
families.voice: Pristine, open, fast solid-state clean: tight lows, glassy bright top, no sag or compression; the 80s chorus clean.

VOLUME.does: Level only - no tube-style breakup to dial in. The real amp's built-in distortion is not modeled.

BRIGHT.does: Roland manual: ON gives 'a bright, clear sound'. Yek always engages it; switch off if the top is harsh.

BASS.does: Conventional bass control; the amp is already tight, so cut only to make room in a mix.

MID.does: Conventional mid control; dip slightly for the glassy 80s clean, raise for body with pedals.

TREBLE.does: Conventional treble control on a naturally bright amp; back it off before blaming a drive pedal for harshness.

model_notes.1008: Amp section only: the famous stereo chorus is not in the amp block - put Chief CE2W (ST) after the amp/cab to recreate it in stereo.

starts.name: flat clean
starts.note: Reported as the Roland manual's clean suggestion (volume 2-4, tone controls at noon); not verified in the manual itself.

starts.name: 80s chorus clean
starts.note: Add Chief CE2W (ST) after the amp and a compressor before it.

boosts.why: Yek: great overdriven tones from a JC-120 with a Tube Screamer; it adds the mids and compression the amp never will.
Full distortion pedals supply all the dirt; Rat-type mids and compression suit a flat, uncompressed clean amp.
Amp-like overdrive with fat lows and strong mids for a clean amp with no breakup of its own.

cabs.why: The JC-120's own 2×12.

known_for: Andy Summers (The Police), Robert Smith, Johnny Marr - 80s chorus cleans
Metallica clean parts ('Fade to Black', 'Welcome Home (Sanitarium)', 'Nothing Else Matters')
Jazz and jazz-rock; 'king of clean'
families.poor_at: Any amp breakup, warmth, sag or touch compression; cannot do 'edge of breakup' by itself.
families.watch_out: It never 'gives': with no compression, pick attack and harsh pedal top-end come through raw. Add a compressor and take all dirt from pedals with their tone rolled back.

families.real: Matchless Chieftain (1990s→), 40 W, 2×EL34 cathode-biased class A, no negative feedback, tube rectifier
families.voice: Thick yet crisp boutique EL34 tone: fat lows, rich complex mids, shimmering top; fair power-amp breakup, very touch-sensitive.

VOLUME.does: First-stage gain: sensitivity and drive. Cleans up well from the guitar's volume when set for overdrive.

BASS.does: Very wide range; too much causes floppiness and loss of definition at high volume (manual). Keep it low.

MID.does: Interactive with BASS and TREBLE; adds body and push.

TREBLE.does: Per the manual it regulates the mid-band and upper mids (the instrument's 'voice'), not just the extreme top.

BRILLIANCE.does: Power-amp high-frequency control: smooths or brings forward the top edge. Reported as up = brighter (unverified).

MASTER.does: Output-amp gain. Maximum = most clean headroom and power-amp feel; lower it and raise VOLUME for dirtier preamp tone.

starts.name: Yek's Boutique 1 setting (Fractal model)
starts.note: 'Master cranked, Hi-Cut around 12 o'clock, low Bass and Input Drive anywhere between 2 and 6.' 4 and 2.5 are mid-points of his ranges.

boosts.why: Low-gain push into an amp that already has rich mids and its own power-amp breakup.
Clean boost with bass/treble trim: more drive without adding the bass the amp punishes.
Bass cut and mid focus tighten the wide, soft low end for leads.

cabs.why: The Chieftain's own 2×12 with Matchless signature drivers.
Chieftain cab with Vintage 30s: more upper-mid cut, tighter.

known_for: Nashville country and session work
Roots and alternative rock; Matchless players such as David Grissom and Kings of Leon
Boutique-amp boom of the early 1990s
families.poor_at: Tight high-gain or scooped tones; the low end flops if BASS is up at volume.
families.watch_out: The BASS knob has far more range than usual: 'more bass' quickly becomes floppy and undefined. Also check BRILLIANCE direction by ear before automating it.

families.real: Matchless DC-30 (C-30 series; Matchless's first design, c. 1989–91→), 30 W, 4×EL84 cathode-biased class A, no negative feedback; Ch1 12AX7, Ch2 EF86
families.voice: A sturdier, hi-fi AC30: chime, shimmer and crunch with more clarity and firmer lows; Ch2 (EF86) is thicker and gainier.

VOLUME.does: Preamp gain; very input-sensitive - dig in and it compresses and gets juicy.

BASS.does: Ch1. Top-Boost-style active stack: BASS and TREBLE are highly interactive.

TREBLE.does: Ch1. Interactive with BASS; the classic chime control.

CUT.does: INVERTED like a Vox cut: power-amp treble cut, up = darker. Subtle below half, strong above; works best with MASTER high.

MASTER.does: Bypassable on the real amp; full up is the open, power-amp-driven tone. Lower it for preamp drive at less level.

TONE.does: Ch2. Six-position switch on the real amp: lowest = thinnest, each step up = thicker. Not a treble knob.

model_notes.1155: Channel 1: two 12AX7s, AC30 Top Boost-type voice; chime and jangle to crunch. The favourite for clean-with-chime.
model_notes.1156: Channel 2: EF86 pentode, more gain and overdrives harder; the 'heavier' channel, shaped by the thickness TONE switch.

starts.name: Yek's Ch1 setting (Fractal model)
starts.note: 'Bass and Treble pretty much at default, Cut to about 3, vary Input Drive between 2 and 8.' Model was made with the master bypassed.

boosts.why: Input boost keeps the chime while adding grit - the usual way to push AC-style amps.
Treble booster into EL84 class-A: more bite and gain, firmer lows.
Mid hump and bass cut for tighter leads from a loose, chimey amp.

cabs.why: The DC-30's own 2×12 (the real combo pairs a modified G12H30 with a Greenback).
Second capture of the same cabinet; pick the one that sits better.

known_for: 'An AC30 that wouldn't break down' - studio and touring workhorse
Nashville session players; country, roots, indie
The amp that started the boutique craze
families.poor_at: Scooped or high-gain tones and big clean headroom at volume.
families.watch_out: Two backwards controls: CUT (up = darker) and Ch2 TONE (up = thicker, not brighter). 'Brighter' here means CUT down or TONE down.

families.real: Morgan SW50 (2010s; built around a ~40-year-old Dumble-style clean amp, widely linked to the Steel String Singer), 50 W, 2×6L6
families.drive_control: MASTER (the amp's Level = power-section gain) with GAIN
families.voice: Mid-60s blackface idea with more clarity and string-to-string definition: loud, big clean with sweet singing sustain.

BRIGHT.does: Brings in top end for dark guitars 'without adding any ice picky highs'.

LOW BOOST.does: Morgan's bass-emphasis switch: moves the mid centre point so more bass comes through. Off for tighter.

GAIN.does: Preamp volume (assumed mapping). Keep moderate for maximum clean headroom.

BASS.does: Interacts with TREBLE for a wide tonal range.

MID.does: Midrange body; more mid than a blackface stack offers.

TREBLE.does: Interacts with BASS for a wide tonal range.

MASTER.does: The amp's Level: power-section gain. Past ~3 o'clock (8) it adds warm, compressed power-amp overdrive.

model_notes.1116: Single channel. QC names differ from the panel: LOW BOOST = bass emphasis; GAIN/MASTER = Volume/Level (assumed).

starts.name: power-amp grit
starts.note: Based on Morgan's description that overdrive arrives past about 3 o'clock on Level.

boosts.why: QC forum: the Morgan is 'such a great pedal platform'; a low-level Klon-type keeps its clarity.
Adds mids and compression to a big, clear, uncompressed clean.
Low-gain Fender-voiced overdrive stacks naturally on a blackface-derived clean.
Fat amp-like drive for when the platform has to cover crunch.

cabs.why: Creambacks: the SW50 combo ships with a Celestion Creamback.
Open-back G12-65s: the Dumble-style clean-amp speaker voice.
EVM12L: maximum headroom, firm lows and clarity for a clean platform.

known_for: Modern clean pedal platform
Players listed for it: Josh Smith, Tosin Abasi, Aaron Marshall
families.poor_at: Amp distortion: only mild power-amp grit at high MASTER; needs pedals for crunch and lead.
families.watch_out: Roles are swapped compared with most amps: the overdrive comes from MASTER (Level), not GAIN. Re-check loudness with OUTPUT after moving MASTER.

families.real: Dumble Overdrive Special (QC: a 1992 'low-plate Skyliner, non-HRM' amp), 6L6; OD channel cascades from the clean preamp
families.drive_control: VOLUME (clean gain, also feeds the OD) and OD CONTENT on the OD channel
families.voice: Fenderish fat clean with strong low-mids; OD channel is thick, mid-heavy, smooth and vocal - sings on single notes, very touch-sensitive.

CHANNEL.does: Clean / OD. The OD stages come after the clean preamp, so VOLUME and the tone stack still shape the OD.

VOLUME.does: Clean-preamp gain. As it rises the tone moves from sparkly upper-mid emphasis to thick, bassy and meaty.

TREBLE.does: Shared stack placed before the OD stages: on the OD channel it works as pre-distortion EQ.

MIDDLE.does: Shared pre-OD stack; more MIDDLE = more signal and thicker drive.

BASS.does: Shared pre-OD stack: bass here goes into the overdrive, so high settings make the OD muddy.

OD CONTENT.does: Amount of OD-channel saturation (forum: 'controls the preamp saturation'); barely changes the tonal balance.

OD VOLUME.does: OD-channel level: balances OD against clean at the same MASTER setting.

MASTER.does: Power-amp level and feel. Users report clean much quieter than OD (MASTER 8-9 to match OD VOLUME 5).

PREAMP.does: Assumed = preamp boost (PAB): bypasses the tone stack for more gain and mids; the EQ knobs then do little.

BRIGHT.does: Adds sparkle; less noticeable as VOLUME goes up. Forum tip: off for single coils, on for humbuckers.

MID.does: Mid boost (a.k.a. Deep): more mids and gain, fatter. Forum tip: on for single coils, off for humbuckers.

EQ.does: Rock / Jazz. Rock is brighter, stronger, more dynamic; Jazz adds low-pass filtering: softer, rounder, lower gain.

model_notes.1176: Non-HRM: no extra Marshall-style tone stack after the OD, so the OD is thicker and more mid-forward. Added in CorOS 3.3.0; 3.3.1 fixed channel-switching bugs.

starts.name: switch set for single coils
starts.note: Forum user jamsden: 'bright off, mid on for single coils, the opposite for double'.

starts.name: fat clean
starts.note: CHANNEL = clean, EQ = Rock, PREAMP off.

starts.name: smooth singing lead
starts.note: CHANNEL = OD, EQ = Rock. Raise OD CONTENT for gain, not BASS or VOLUME.

boosts.why: Into the clean channel: mid focus and bass cut keep the cascaded OD from getting woolly.
Low-gain push on the clean channel for edge-of-breakup while leaving the OD channel for leads.
Bass and treble controls let you trim what goes into an amp whose EQ sits before its overdrive.

cabs.why: G12-65s are the speaker for the Robben Ford tone; Neural DSP says the Two Rock cabs pair well with this model.
EVM12L: the other classic Dumble speaker - loud, clear, firm lows.
A QC forum user's preferred cab for this model (with 412 Cornfield V30).

known_for: Robben Ford, Larry Carlton, Carlos Santana, Eric Johnson, John Mayer, Joe Bonamassa, Keith Urban
Smooth, vocal blues/fusion lead tone and fat clean
families.poor_at: Power chords and tight riffing (the thick mids smear), scooped or aggressive tones, metal.
families.watch_out: The OD is cascaded: clean VOLUME and BASS decide how muddy it gets. Keep BASS low and VOLUME moderate, and expect a big clean/OD level gap to fix with OD VOLUME.

families.real: Mesa/Boogie Lone Star (original 'Classic', introduced mid-2000s), 100/50 W switchable, 4×6L6, built-in variac 'Tweed' power mode
families.drive_control: GAIN (clean models); DRIVE with GAIN (drive models)
families.voice: Polished blackface-style clean with rounder, fatter low-mids and big headroom; Drive channel is smooth, thick and singing.

GAIN.does: Gain AND tone: low (0-4) bright and 3-D, middle (4-7) warmer and fuller - the sweet spot, high = saturated lows, soft attack.

DRIVE.does: Drive models. Extra cascaded gain; balance it against GAIN (GAIN below DRIVE = brighter, thinner).

TREBLE.does: Dominant control, first in the stack: high TREBLE starves MID and BASS and adds gain. Sweet spot about 4-6.5.

MID.does: Low (0-4) = scooped, girthy, softer feel; 4.5-6.5 fills in with focused attack; higher = stiffer, more forward, more gain.

BASS.does: Very powerful. Mesa's rule: as GAIN goes up, turn BASS down to keep the attack tight and dynamic.

PRESENCE.does: High-cut at the END OF THE PREAMP (not power-amp feedback): lower = darker and more compressed, fat for leads.

MASTER.does: Channel master; Mesa suggests staying in its sensible range (about 2-7).

EQ.does: Assumed = voicing switch Normal / Thick / Thicker: lowers the treble frequency and adds gain there; Normal = blackface.

model_notes.1101: Clean, 50 W, normal power: earlier power-amp give than 100 W.
model_notes.1102: Clean, 50 W, Tweed (variac ~93 V): spongier, scoopier, clips earliest - 'old school clip' sounds.
model_notes.1103: Clean, 100 W, normal power: maximum headroom and firmest lows; the pedal-platform choice.
model_notes.1104: Clean, 100 W, Tweed: big but softer and scoopier.
model_notes.1105: Drive, 50 W, normal power: singing lead with more power-amp compression.
model_notes.1106: Drive, 50 W, Tweed: loosest, most vintage-feeling lead.
model_notes.1107: Drive, 100 W, normal power: tightest, boldest lead of the four.
model_notes.1108: Drive, 100 W, Tweed: big lead with a spongier attack.

starts.name: blackface-style clean
starts.note: EQ on the Normal voicing. Follows the manual's regions: GAIN low-to-middle, TREBLE in its 4-6.5 sweet spot, MID scooped.

starts.name: roots clean / old-school clip (50 W Tweed models)
singing lead (Drive models)
starts.note: Manual: best lead sounds have PRESENCE low; reduce BASS as gain rises. QC wiki: add rock edge with TREBLE, then cut MID and BASS.

boosts.why: BB Preamp-type boost with bass/treble: trims the big low end and adds mid gain for the singing lead this amp is known for.
Bass cut before the amp fixes the low-end bloom that arrives with gain.
On the clean models it behaves like a blackface: a low-gain mid push for edge of breakup.

cabs.why: Mesa cab with Celestion Black Shadows - the family of the C90s Mesa fits to the Lone Star.
Mesa 2×12 with Vintage 30s: tighter, more upper-mid cut for the Drive models.
Open-back Fender 2×12 pushes the clean models further toward blackface sparkle.

known_for: Andy Timmons' clean and lead tones
QC forum favourite for 'a great Fender Blackface tone' (100 W clean)
Blues, country, fusion, instrumental rock
families.poor_at: Tight high-gain rhythm: gain brings in a lot of bass that the BASS knob barely removes. Not a metal amp.
families.watch_out: More GAIN makes it darker and bassier, not just dirtier, and at high GAIN the tone knobs stop working. Keep GAIN in the middle, lower BASS as gain rises, and use PRESENCE as a smoothing control.

families.real: Bogner Shiva 20th Anniversary (KT88, 90 W) - clean channel
families.voice: Beefy, warm, slightly dark clean with big KT88 headroom; shimmers once Treble, Bright and Presence come up; crunch only near the top.

BRIGHT.does: Bright switch; less effective the higher GAIN is set.

GAIN.does: Channel volume: stays clean until very high; 7+ with MASTER at 7 gives a crunchy overdrive.

BASS.does: Bass of the clean stack; the tone controls stay in circuit on the 20th Anniversary.

MID.does: Midrange body of the clean channel.

TREBLE.does: Bogner taper: noon is dark (about a Marshall's treble at 1). Run it 7-9 without fear.

MASTER.does: Higher = beefier clean with more power-amp body (Yek always raises it, around 7).

PRESENCE.does: Power-amp top end; raise it with TREBLE for bite and clarity.

DEPTH.does: The amp's 'Excursion' (power-amp damping): up = bigger, looser bottom. Keep low at high volume.

model_notes.1117: KT88 version has less gain and more headroom than EL34 Shivas. The real amp's clean Boost is not exposed as a parameter.

starts.name: Yek's beefy clean (Fractal model)
starts.note: 'Turn up Input Drive and Master to 7. Also turn up Treble and Presence to add bite and clarity.' On the real amp this is also where crunch begins.

boosts.why: High-headroom clean takes a low-gain mid push well; its TREBLE control offsets the dark voicing.
Mid hump and bass cut focus the beefy low end for leads.
Amp-like crunch on top of a clean that will not break up until nearly full.

cabs.why: Celestion Classic Lead 80s - one of the two speakers Bogner fits to Shiva cabs.
Bogner cabinet with Vintage 30s, the Shiva's other stock speaker.
2×12 Vintage 30 alternative in a combo-like size.

known_for: Warm, beefy boutique clean from a two-channel rock amp
Rock, alternative and blues players who want one amp for clean and thick gain
families.poor_at: Glassy scooped Fender sparkle at default settings; early breakup (it stays clean almost to the top).
families.watch_out: It only seems dark because of the pot tapers. Set TREBLE and PRESENCE by ear, well past noon, before reaching for EQ.

families.real: Friedman BE-100 (HBE100) - clean channel; 100 W, 4×EL34, modded-Plexi lineage
families.voice: Chimey Plexi-style clean: brighter, firmer and more mid-present than a blackface Fender, with EL34 snap and little scoop.

BRIGHT.does: Three-position switch that varies the overall brightness of the clean channel only; choose by ear.

BASS.does: Clean-channel bass (there is no mid control). Manual start: 5.

TREBLE.does: Clean-channel treble. Manual start: 5.

VOLUME.does: The clean channel's only level control (no separate master): turn up to taste; high settings add grit.

PRESENCE.does: Global: adds or removes brightness in the upper mids and lower highs; 5 is the neutral start.

model_notes.1027: The utility clean of a high-gain rock amp; the BE and HBE channels (1028, 1082) belong to the high-gain research set.

starts.name: manual starting point
starts.note: Friedman manual as quoted: 'set the Treble and Bass at 5 and turn the Volume up to taste', then experiment with the Bright switch; presence start '5'.

boosts.why: The BE-OD is this amp's dirty channel as a pedal: turns the clean channel into BE-style crunch.
The BE100 'was designed to take pedals and loves boosts'; low-gain push for edge of breakup.
Mid-focused overdrive on a firm, bright clean for classic-rock leads.

cabs.why: Friedman 4×12s use G12M, G12H or V30s; Greenbacks give the warmer Plexi-clean voice.
Vintage 30 4×12: more upper-mid cut and tightness.
G12H-type Creambacks in a 2×12: firmer lows, less compression.

known_for: Clean channel of the BE-100 used by Jerry Cantrell, Steve Stevens, Phil X and other rock players
Rock rigs that need one bright, firm clean next to high gain
families.poor_at: Lush scooped Fender cleans or a big soft low end; only bass and treble to shape it.
families.watch_out: No mid knob and no master on this channel: VOLUME changes loudness and breakup together, so set the feel with VOLUME and level-match with OUTPUT.
